label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss) is TP: User input 'param' flows directly into the XSS sink at L84-L85 ('... + param + ...') where the entire constructed string is printed to the response writer without sanitization. Although encodeForHTML is called on parts of the string (the attribute values), the 'param' portion remains unsanitized and attacker-controlled. Alert 2 (java/ldap-injection) is TP: User input 'param' flows directly into the LDAP filter at L59 ('...|(uid=' + param + ...)'), creating an injection vector.

evidence.note: XSS sink prints raw user input 'param' without escaping
LDAP filter includes raw user input 'param' causing injection
